A SELF-PACED INVESTIGATION · ABOUT 2 HOURS

Good for everyone?
Look a little closer.

A club recommendation system looks successful on average. Your job: find who it leaves behind, change the rules, and defend your decisions.

01 Investigate · 40 min02 Experiment · 60 min03 Reflect · 15 min

01 / FOLLOW THE EVIDENCE

Start with a prediction

Student 9 likes poetry and can attend only morning meetings. The original system uses 30% interest, 10% schedule, and 60% popularity. Which club will rank first? Why?

First case hintCampus Connect scores 60 for popularity despite no interest match or schedule compatibility. Poetry Circle scores 30 + 10 + 4.8 = 44.8. Can popularity overwhelm usefulness?

Next: inspect Student 8 without a hint. Then find another failure and record evidence below.

02 / CHANGE ONE THING

Make a defensible improvement

Change one setting from the last run, predict the effect, then test. Weights are normalized by their sum; zero total weight is invalid.

Scoring rules

Visible validation results

40 synthetic profiles. Groups overlap. Empty recommendations count as unsuitable.

Recommendation variety

Trace a recommendation

Club / meetingInterestSchedulePopularityTotalSuitable label

Score = 100 × (interest weight × match + schedule weight × compatibility + popularity weight × popularity) ÷ sum of weights. Interest match is the fraction of student interests in the club tags. Schedule is 0 or 1. Ties use club ID.

Your experiment log

03 / EXPLAIN THE TRADEOFF

Submit your reasoning

Export includes your last tested settings, prediction, diagnosis, results, and decision log. Staff evaluate unseen profiles offline; hidden results are never returned here.

Published assessment rubric

Decision log 40% · Diagnosis 25% · Hidden evaluation 25% · Reflection 10%.

Example hidden-evaluation bands (of 25): 25 if overall improves ≥10 percentage points and neither subgroup declines; 20 if overall improves and neither subgroup declines; 15 if overall is unchanged and a subgroup improves with no subgroup decline; 10 if all rates match baseline; otherwise 5. Staff assess reasoning separately. These are prototype bands for a pilot, not a validated course grading policy.

Synthetic data only. No accounts, live student data, or model training. Progress is saved in this browser when storage is available. Pilot the exercise to verify the proposed 1–3 hour completion time.
